top.title: Liverpool is Arsenal’s main rival for World Cup teenage sensation
top.description: Liverpool is Arsenal’s main rival for World Cup teenage sensation Gilberto Mora has attracted Arsenal’s attention after impressing for Mexico at the 2026 World Cup , where he was the youngest player in the competition. Despite his age, the teenager produced some encouraging performances and stood out among the players representing his country. Mora has been regarded as one of the finest young talents in world football for some time, which helped him earn a place in the Mexico squad and receive playing opportunities during the tournament. His performances have further increased interest in his future, with several clubs reportedly monitoring his development . The youngster currently plays for Tijuana, but the Mexican club may struggle to keep hold of him if interest from major European teams continues to grow. Arsenal are among those keen to secure his signature as they look to add another promising young player to their squad. Arsenal step up interest in Mexican youngster The Gunners reportedly view Mora as one of the most exciting young players they could sign and are not keen to wait until the summer before making their move. They are considering an approach in the January transfer window as they look to get ahead of their competitors. However, Arsenal are not alone in the Premier League race for the teenager. According to Sport Witness , Liverpool are also interested in signing him and could compete with the Gunners for his services. The Reds have reportedly followed Mora for some time and have maintained their interest in bringing him to England. They are also considering making an approach in January, meaning Arsenal could face competition from another major Premier League club. (Photo by Azael Rodriguez/Getty Images) Mora faces decision over his next move With both clubs reportedly interested, Mora could have an important decision to make about the next stage of his career. A move to the Premier League would represent a significant opportunity, but he will need to consider which destination offers the right environment for his development. Arsenal will hope their interest and plans to move early can help them secure an agreement, while Liverpool will also be keen to make their long-standing admiration count. For now, Mora remains a Tijuana player, but the growing attention surrounding him could make the January transfer window an important period for his future. top.title: December full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Cold Moon
top.description: null The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon).. According to the late, great astronomer Fred Espenak , the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026! When to see the December full moon The full Cold Supermoon will make for a spectacular sight when it rises over the eastern horizon at sunset on Dec. 23, mere hours before reaching maximum illumination. Remember to use Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location. Earth's satellite may appear larger than normal while close to the horizon. This is partly because it is near perigee, when it appears subtly larger in the night sky, but also because of a phenomenon called the moon illusion, which tricks us into perceiving the moon to be bigger than it actually is while in the presence of foreground objects. A yellow full moon rises over Italy. (Image credit: Photo by Lorenzo Di Cola/NurPhoto via Getty Images) The moon may also adopt a striking golden or orange hue around moonrise and moonset. When the moon is low on the horizon, its light travels through more of Earth's atmopshere, scattering shorter, bluer wavelengths of light and allowing longer, redder wavelengths to reach our eyes. top.description: Manchester City's owners have been sent a warning by football regulator David Kogan -Credit:Tom Jenkins, Getty Images Football regulator David Kogan insists he "has the stomach" to take on Manchester City's owners. City are contesting the ruling that they violated more than 100 Premier League financial regulations, and should that appeal fail, they are likely to face further scrutiny from the newly established Independent Football Regulator. The regulator holds the authority to strip City's ownership hierarchy of control, and Kogan assured MPs on the Digital, Culture, Media and Sport select committee that he will remain immune to any political interference. Florian Wirtz on Liverpool struggles after record transfer and impact of Jürgen Klopp Alejandro Garnacho casts doubt over Aston Villa future after taking drastic action City fans continue to support the board -Credit:Offside via Getty Images Kogan said, via The Mirror : "If you look at the specific sanctions we can impose, we have everything from deciding there is not sufficient evidence to take any action or removing them as directors and from any involvement with the club or English football going forward. But let's be blunt. The two things I was asked about were: would we be subject to political pressure and did we have the stomach to take action? "The answers are: We won't be. And we have the stomach for that. We can't be an independent football regulator and ignore our duties because the club is of a certain size. "Would I, given my choice with an organization that has a relatively new, fairly young staff that's been going for less than a year, would I have chosen to have this particular issue in our laps this early? Well, probably not. But the truth is, if we don't act, assuming those circumstances are triggered, if we don't act, what is the purpose of having a football regulator?" Prime Minister Andy Burnham has previously stated he would be "really concerned" if the fallout led to Abu Dhabi's Sheikh Mansour walking away from the club, with fears also raised that the situation could impact UK trade agreements with the United Arab Emirates. Kogan, however, was emphatic: "We will have to act appropriately. And that is the only test, not the politics around it, not the place where it came from, not the size of the club. It is the only test because without that, you cannot have an effective regulator." top.title: Baylor zeroes in on Jeff Traylor as next football coach. Why a deal could move quickly
top.description: Once it fired Dave Aranda , Baylor conducted a nationwide search for its next football coach. Turns out, the Bears have zeroed in their search some 200 miles from their Waco, Texas, campus — in San Antonio. Nine people with direct knowledge of Baylor’s search process, from college coaches to NFL assistants and industry agents, told USA TODAY Sports in recent days that Baylor has dialed in its search on Texas-San Antonio coach Jeff Traylor. The people requested anonymity due to the sensitivity of the situation. No deal has been finalized but those individuals stressed that, barring unforeseen circumstances, it was expected that Baylor would seek to move forward with Traylor before week’s end. Texas-San Antonio hosts Tulsa on Friday, Nov. 27. The Roadrunners are in first place in the American Conference and would clinch a berth in the title game with a win. They could still reach the game with a loss. The Baylor search party wanted to focus the process on candidates with deep Lone Star State roots, and Taylor’s credentials are hard to match. A Gilbert, Texas, native who played his college football Stephen F. Austin, Traylor merely has spent all but two years of his coaching career since 1989 inside the Texas border. Baylor talked to a bevy of candidates, including top coordinators and sitting head coaches, including UNLV’s Dan Mullen, per people with direct knowledge of the search, but always targeted a candidate with Texas ties. Former Heisman Trophy-winning quarterback Robert Griffin III also was part of the search; three different people told USA TODAY Sports that RG3 pushed hard for an opportunity to coach at his alma mater. In addition to his three Texas high school state championships at Gilmer High School, Traylor coached in an assistant role at both the University of Texas and SMU before he logged two years at Arkansas. For the fourth time in seven seasons, Traylor has won nine or more games – and he’s never closed his time atop the Roadrunners with a losing record. In addition to three consecutive bowl wins, Traylor has amassed an overall mark of 60-28 to include an 23-5 mark in the 2022-23 seasons. Traylor, per terms of his contract obtained. USA TODAY Sports, would owe the school $4 million if he exits for another FBS job before Dec. 31, 2026. top.title: Stuttgart wasteful again as Sucic and Lautaro seal Inter win
top.description: Stuttgart wasteful again as Sucic and Lautaro seal Inter win As Stuttgart looked to get back to winning ways in Europe following the defeat to Galatasaray, they could hardly have gotten off to a more encouraging start, with the visitors testing Italian giants Inter in the early stages. Maximilian Mittelstädt fired in a teasing ball after six minutes, flying a matter of centimetres past the foot of Ermedin Demirovic. The Bosnian forward, and skipper on the night, would be presented with an opportunity again just over a minute later, linking up well with Chris Führich before seeing a shot blocked. Führich, who was Stuttgart's best player in Istanbul before the international break, remained at the heart of proceedings, seeing an effort well saved by Josep Martinez on the half-volley, before Djed Spence was denied by Dennis Seimen at the other end following the resulting corner. And after the strong Stuttgart start, it would be all Inter for the rest of the half, with Marcus Thuram and Nicolo Barella having the best chances - the former hitting the side netting after a poor Finn Jeltsch backpass, while Barella struck the post with a lovely outside-of-the-boot effort inside the box. Tailing off after the positive start, Stuttgart were looking to avoid the sloppiness that plagued the half outside of the opening 15 minutes. However, after the opening minutes matched the theme of the first half, Inter would be presented with a huge chance to open the scoring, when Federico Dimarco's cross struck the hand of Josha Vagnoman, resulting in a penalty for the hosts after a VAR check. And with a hop and a skip, Petar Sucic would wrong-foot Seimen, sending the ball straight down the middle and giving the Nerazzurri the lead on home soil. Reacting well, Nikolas Nartey would see an effort somehow saved off the line from a corner, while the visitors began to finally regain some of their attacking impetus. Führich and Vagnoman were withdrawn, replaced by Deniz Undav and Jamie Leweling, while Angelo Stiller and Luca Jaquez followed, But just as they were beginning to threaten, with wing-back Mittelstädt calling for a penalty at one end, Inter went up the other end and doubled their lead through the ever-talismanic Lautaro Martinez, who hammered home off the post, catching a bouncing ball ever so sweetly to net his third goal in three Champions League outings. Sebastian Hoeneß cannot argue that the three points deservedly stay in Milan, but once again, he will have to deal with the frustrating topic of his side once again being wasteful. As a result, Stuttgart sit 17th in the standings, with a strong run to the end of the league phase in need, starting with the visit of Lille in two weeks time.

top.title: 2 goals, 84% passing accuracy: Bruno Fernandes’ efforts go to waste as Man United held 2-2 by Sporting
top.description: 2 goals, 84% passing accuracy: Bruno Fernandes’ efforts go to waste as Man United held 2-2 by Sporting Manchester United were held to a 2-2 draw by Sporting at the Estádio José Alvalade on Wednesday, 25 November, in the Champions League. A Bruno Fernandes brace was cancelled out by two goals from Luis Suárez in an entertaining game that earned Mauricio Pochettino his first points since taking charge at Old Trafford. The Argentine made four changes to the team that was thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield last weekend in the Premier League. Matheus Cunha missed the game due to suspension, while Diogo Dalot, Matthijs de Ligt and Patrick Dorgu all dropped to the bench. Harry Maguire and Noussair Mazraoui came into the team, starting at the back alongside Leny Yoro and Lisandro Martínez. Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans retained their place in the starting XI, continuing their partnership in midfield. Bruno Fernandes continued in the No. 10 position, with Bryan Mbeumo moving to the left forward role and Amad starting on the right. Joshua Zirkzee started for the first time this season, operating in the No. 9 role. United secure hard-fought draw United had a bright start, but Sporting gradually got a grip on the game. Martínez conceded a penalty, which was saved by Senne Lammens in the 30th minute. However, the Belgian conceded a penalty moments later, which was successfully converted by Luis Suárez in the 33rd minute. The visitors pushed for an equaliser late in the second half, but went into the break trailing 1-0. Martínez made amends early in the second half, winning a penalty which Fernandes converted in the 48th minute. The United skipper then scored a second two minutes later, giving his team the lead. Sporting pushed for an equaliser and finally found one through Suárez in the 80th minute following a Lammens error. United did have the ball in the back of the net late in the game but it was ruled out by VAR. The game ended 2-2, despite the best efforts of Fernandes, who sizzled on his return to his former hunting ground. Page 1 of 5 1 2 3 4 5 Fernandes decisive on Sporting return Bruno Fernandes played the entire 90 minutes on his return to the Estádio José Alvalade, before being replaced in the second half injury time, managing 49 touches of the ball. The Portuguese maestro attempted 44 passes with an 84% accuracy rate. The 32-year-old attempted two crosses and one long ball, but none of them found a teammate. Surprisingly, Fernandes did not register a single key pass in the game. The Portuguese attempted two tackles and was dribbled past once in the game. top.title: Pavlovic drops clanger as Lille seal upset win vs Bayern
top.description: Pavlovic drops clanger as Lille seal upset win vs Bayern On a night in which Bayern Munich were looking to reset the mood after a week of injuries and controversy behind the scenes, Vincent Kompany would be left to field a far-from-ideal lineup with multiple stars watching on from the sidelines. Konrad Laimer's versatility has been well-documented throughout his years in the Bundesliga, but few could have predicted that the Austrian would be the man to start up top in Lille. And much to their credit, the German record champions did not have to get out of second gear in the first half, despite the rather makeshift lineup. Dayot Upamecano would open the scoring in Northern France after just 15 minutes, rising highest to meet Tom Bischof's corner to head home from six yards out. From then on, Bayern were cruising, before the half-time break completely turned the tide. Lille would see an equaliser disallowed after just a minute of second-half football, when Ayase Ueda bundled over Joshua Kimmich in the build-up to the latter scoring an own goal. But the Mastiffs remained well in the occasion before Ueda netted an equaliser in the 60th minute, and it is hard to say it wasn't deserved after a much better start to the second period. And within a matter of moments, the hosts would take the lead when Ethan Mbappe raced through on goal just to find the post, before Aleksandar Pavlovic bundled the ball into his own net following an attempt to control the ball he will not want to see again. Out of nowhere, Lille had a huge upset win in their sights, while Bayern turned to Luis Diaz and Jamal Musiala from the bench, and campus graduates Tim Binder and Noah Codjo-Evore made their European debuts. Soriba Diaoune missed a huge chance to add a third on the volley five minutes out from time, ensuring that the final moments were going to remain uncomfortable for the hosts. But, as much as the makeshift Bayern frontline threw at Lille in the closing stages, the French side were able to hold on for what is a huge win - their first of the Champions League season. Bayern, on the other hand, tasted defeat for the first time in all competitions this term, seeing the rather strange week continue for the record champions.

nigeria.title: Nigeria Joins Global Pact To Protect Marine Biodiversity, Unlock Ocean Resources
nigeria.description: Nigeria has secured a significant international milestone for the country’s marine and blue economy, following its formal ratification of a landmark United Nations treaty on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. The historic instrument of ratification was deposited on behalf of President Bola Tinubu by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. ﻿ Speaking at the ceremony, Ibrahim highlighted the economic and strategic importance of the agreement to Nigeria, noting that it would expand the country’s opportunities to benefit from ocean resources through greater participation in the governance of the high seas. The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty, provides a framework for the protection, management and sustainable use of marine resources in areas beyond national jurisdiction. For Nigeria, a coastal nation along the Gulf of Guinea, the agreement marks a significant step towards strengthening its marine economy, protecting biodiversity, supporting fisheries and unlocking opportunities in emerging ocean-based industries. A major implication of the ratification is Nigeria’s plan to develop a proposal for the establishment of a highly protected marine area on the high seas. The initiative is also expected to strengthen efforts to conserve marine ecosystems while promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits from ocean resources, particularly for developing countries. Nigeria signed the BBNJ Agreement on May 3, 2024. Following the deposit of its instrument of ratification, the agreement will enter into force for Nigeria on December 24, 2026. This will enable the country to participate as a full Party at the first Conference of the Parties, scheduled to open on January 11, 2027. At the ceremony, Ibrahim acknowledged Evelyn Campos Sanchez, Officer-in-Charge of the United Nations Treaty Section, for receiving Nigeria’s instrument of ratification. Nigeria’s commitment to the agreement is further reinforced by the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, alongside the adoption of a National Blue Economy Policy and a national roadmap for implementing the treaty. As a party to the agreement, Nigeria will continue to advocate for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from marine genetic resources and digital sequence information. The country will also push for stronger capacity-building initiatives and the transfer of marine technology to African and other developing nations. Ambassador Ibrahim further noted Nigeria’s support for the establishment and effective operation of a Special Fund with adequate and predictable resources to enable developing countries to implement the agreement. nigeria.title: 4 African countries to have produced Miss Universe winners
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African contestants have earned the Miss Universe crown six times, across four countries. South Africa leads with three wins, while Namibia, Botswana and Angola have each won once. The titleholders claimed their crowns between 1978 and 2019, giving each country a place in the pageant’s history. The latest milestone achieved by an African nation is from Miss Universe 2024 where Nigeria’s Chidimma Adetshina finished as first runner-up and was named Miss Universe Africa and Oceania. That was a notable result for Nigeria, but it did not add another country to the list of African Miss Universe winners as the overall crown went to Denmark’s Victoria Kjær Theilvig. Here are the four African countries ranked by the number of Miss Universe crowns their representatives have won. South Africa: three wins South Africa has won the title three times. Margaret Gardiner became the country’s first winner in 1978. Demi-Leigh Nel-Peters won in 2017, and Zozibini Tunzi followed in 2019. Tunzi was the third South African winner and the first Black South African woman to earn the crown. Namibia: one win Michelle McLean won Miss Universe in 1992, becoming the first and, according to the pageant’s official profile, so far the only Namibian woman to win. The win came two years after Namibia gained independence in 1990. Botswana: one win Mpule Kwelagobe won the title in 1999. She remains the only woman from Botswana to be crowned Miss Universe, according to the pageant’s official legacy page. Angola: one win Leila Lopes won Miss Universe in 2011, becoming the first Angolan titleholder. The official Miss Universe legacy page records her win and notes that she later served as national director of Miss Angola Universe. nigeria.title: Gordon hits brace as Barcelona cruise to 4-1 Sabah win
nigeria.description: Anthony Gordon struck twice as Barcelona eased to a 4-1 victory at Sabah in the Champions League to boost their chances of a top eight league phase finish. Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus also found the net for the Spanish champions as they triumphed in Azerbaijan at the Baku Olympic stadium. The Catalan giants were without teenage star Lamine Yamal for the long journey east, but found their rhythm after a slow start to claim the three points and a fourth win from five matches in the Champions League. Despite Yamal’s absence, Barca coach Hansi Flick also chose to rest Raphinha, handing Jesus a rare start up front since his summer move from Arsenal. Khayal Aliyev fired a good early chance straight at Joan Garcia as Sabah threatened in attack, against Barca’s notably fragile defence. Barca midfielder Pedri was denied at the other end before Sabah hit the crossbar, with Ivan Lepinjica’s looping effort beating Garcia but not the woodwork. Gordon broke the deadlock in the 31st minute after Sabah goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov pushed Adeyemi’s cross into his path. The England international netted four goals in his prior appearance in Baku, against Qarabag for Newcastle last season, and was Barca’s brightest player. Gordon had a second effort ruled out for offside against Jesus in the build-up, before the interval. The winger struck six minutes into the second half after Jesus’s effort was saved and the rebound came his way. It was the first of three goals in 10 minutes for the Catalan giants, with Adeyemi notching after Alejandro Balde crossed for him. Jesus bundled home Barca’s fourth of the night from almost on the goalline after Pokatilov parried Jules Kounde’s header. Barcelona had kept a clean sheet against Aston Villa in their previous European clash, after conceding in the previous 18, but were unable to add another. Joy-Lance Mickels pulled one back for Champions League debutants Sabah with a cool finish after Christian Nwachukwu pulled the ball across for him. Adeyemi crashed a shot off the bar as Barcelona threatened sporadically in the final stages without adding to their already ample tally. nigeria.description: Former Minister of Transportation, Rotimi Amaechi, has congratulated former Vice President Atiku Abubakar on his 80th birthday, saying Nigeria needs leaders with the experience, courage and capacity to address its economic and security challenges. Amaechi, in a birthday message issued on Wednesday, described Atiku as a distinguished statesman, entrepreneur, philanthropist and patriot whose contributions to Nigeria’s political, economic and social development remained significant. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), turned 80 on Wednesday. Amaechi, a former governor of Rivers State, recalled Atiku’s tenure as Vice President between 1999 and 2007, noting his role in consolidating the Fourth Republic and driving economic reforms. He also highlighted Atiku’s leadership of the National Council on Privatisation, saying his contributions reflected his belief in private-sector development and an enabling business environment. The former minister also commended Atiku’s entrepreneurial investments in agriculture, logistics and real estate, as well as his establishment of the American University of Nigeria, Yola. He said the university reflected Atiku’s commitment to education and human capital development. Amaechi further acknowledged Atiku’s philanthropic activities, particularly his support for educational opportunities for disadvantaged Nigerians and young people affected by the Chibok tragedy. Looking ahead to the 2027 general election, Amaechi said Nigeria required leadership capable of restoring economic confidence, strengthening national security, improving education and healthcare, and ensuring reliable electricity supply. He also backed Atiku’s proposed reintroduction of petroleum production subsidy, arguing that the policy could reduce transportation costs and ease the burden of rising prices on households. According to Amaechi, Nigeria needs a people-centred development agenda that prioritises entrepreneurship, technological innovation, human capital development and private-sector-led growth. He expressed confidence in Atiku’s ambition to contest the 2027 presidential election, saying the country needed leaders who understood its challenges and were prepared to take difficult decisions. Amaechi also called for a Nigeria where young people could find opportunities at home, farmers could prosper, businesses could grow and citizens could access quality education regardless of their backgrounds. nigeria.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The Federal Government has ordered an investigation into the deaths of three condemned inmates at the Oke-Kura Custodial Centre in Ilorin, Kwara State, following a jailbreak attempt last week. The Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, who ordered the investigation, described the deaths as unfortunate and vowed that anyone found culpable would face the full weight of the law. The minister, who visited the facility on Wednesday to assess the situation, also expressed concern that more than 70 condemned inmates at the centre had spent over 10 years on death row, attributing the prolonged stay to delays by state authorities in exercising their powers to grant clemency or commute death sentences. The minister was represented during the visit by the Comptroller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service, Mr Sylvester Nwakuche, who briefed journalists after inspecting the facility. Nwakuche said he returned to Ilorin on the minister’s directive to investigate reports surrounding the incident and assess the condition of the facility. According to him, seven condemned inmates attempted to breach the security of the custodial centre during the jailbreak, but only two succeeded in escaping. He said the remaining five were apprehended and returned to custody, but three subsequently died. “Two succeeded in making their way out of the facility, while the remaining five could not. They were taken back, but unfortunately, we were informed that three out of the five who could not escape lost their lives. “That is an unfortunate incident, and the minister wanted us to come immediately to assess the situation,” he said. The Comptroller-General said a team had been constituted to investigate the deaths, adding that the inquiry would involve clinical, medical and intelligence processes. He assured that the two escaped inmates would be rearrested, regardless of how long it took. Nwakuche also disclosed that more than 70 condemned inmates were being held at the Oke-Kura facility, with some having spent over a decade on death row. He described the situation as a major challenge, noting that the colonial-era facility was accommodating nearly 685 inmates and was severely overcrowded. He said the problem extended beyond Ilorin, disclosing that more than 4,000 inmates were on death row across correctional facilities nationwide. The Comptroller-General appealed to state governors to exercise their constitutional powers by considering the commutation of death sentences to life imprisonment, where appropriate. The American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, H.R. 8957, was filed with amendments as House Report 119-894 and placed on the Union Calendar as Calendar No. 789 on Nov. 24, according to congressional records. The committee had voted 28-21 to advance the bill at a Sept. 16 markup. Rep. Nick Begich, an Alaska Republican, introduced the bill on May 21. It now lists 23 cosponsors, including Rep. Jared Golden, a Maine Democrat, with Reps. Byron Donalds and Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida added on Nov. 24. What the amended bill does The reported text directs the Treasury secretary to set up a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a separate Digital Asset Stockpile within 180 days of the law taking effect. Bitcoin owned by the federal government would move into the reserve, while other digital assets would go to the stockpile. The centerpiece is a lock-up. Treasury would have to hold all bitcoin deposited in the reserve for at least 20 years after enactment, and during that period no reserve bitcoin could be “sold, swapped, auctioned, encumbered, or otherwise disposed of for any purpose.” After the 20 years, the Treasury secretary could recommend selling up to 10% of the reserve in any two-year period. Two years before the holding period ends, Treasury would have to send Congress recommendations on whether to keep holding or begin a gradual release. Federal agencies would have 60 days after enactment to give Treasury a full accounting of the bitcoin and other digital assets they hold or have seized. Until the reserve is set up, agencies could not sell those coins except for national security, when required by law or a court, or to return assets to crime victims. The bill also creates a Proof of Reserve system. Treasury would publish an annual report on total holdings, transactions and control of private keys, checked by an independent auditor with expertise in cryptographic attestations, while the Government Accountability Office would provide oversight. States could choose to store their own bitcoin in segregated accounts inside the federal reserve, keeping title to the coins and the right to withdraw them. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypto Tax Data Sharing Starting in 2028 Switzerland’s Federal Council has approved 57 countries and territories with which the country plans to automatically share tax information on crypto users starting in 2028, extending its long-standing bank data exchange to bitcoin and other digital assets. The list includes all European Union member states, the United Kingdom and various G20 countries, the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) said in a release on Wednesday. The exchange will run under the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, known as CARF. With the decision, Switzerland intends to implement the crypto exchange at the same time as other global asset management centers, according to the release. The government did not name the 57 jurisdictions beyond those broad groups, and it did not publish the full list alongside the announcement. Exchanges only with partners that qualify Data will not flow to every name on the list. An exchange will take place only if a partner jurisdiction wants to swap information with Switzerland and meets the conditions of the OECD standard, in particular its requirements on confidentiality and data security. Before any financial account or crypto data changes hands, the Federal Council will run a targeted check of whether each partner complies with OECD standards. It will rely on a review mechanism Parliament approved on Sept. 28, 2026, which covers both the older exchange of bank account data and the new crypto exchange. The domestic legal basis for the crypto exchange took effect on Jan. 1, 2026. Earlier this month, though, the SIF said the framework could not be implemented before Jan. 1, 2027, because the partner list still needed approval and notifications had to go to the OECD. The rules do not apply this year. The Council also approved Armenia and Rwanda as new partners for the exchange of financial account information, with first exchanges due in 2028, and signed off on two notifications needed to carry out the exchange. Both partner lists were broadly supported during public consultations in 2024 and 2025, the government said. Down from 74 partners The final list is shorter than first planned. In June 2025, the Federal Council proposed 74 countries relevant to the crypto market, including all EU states, the UK and most G20 members. That plan left out the United States and Saudi Arabia, and it targeted a 2026 start with first data exchanges in 2027. Wednesday’s release did not say which countries were dropped or whether the U.S. is now on the list. The U.S. has committed to begin CARF exchanges by 2029, according to the OECD’s Global Forum, which lists Switzerland among 27 jurisdictions aiming for first exchanges by 2028. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Passports, Bank Accounts and Wallet Addresses South Korean crypto exchange Bithumb said Wednesday that an October hack of its internal systems exposed more people and far more personal data than it first disclosed, including passport numbers, bank account numbers and crypto wallet addresses. The exchange also said the intruder had access for about 15 days before being shut out, not the roughly one hour it reported last month. In an updated notice posted Nov. 25, Bithumb said a follow-up review of the breach of Daou Office, its internal mobile groupware system, turned up additional affected people and additional types of data. The company said the new findings stem from the same incident it disclosed on Oct. 29. Bithumb breach ran for 15 days Bithumb now says an unauthorized outside party accessed the groupware system from 1:49 p.m. on Oct. 12 to 3:22 p.m. on Oct. 27, Korea time, and took personal information and files stored there. That is a sharp change from its first account. Bithumb had said the hack lasted about an hour, from 11:28 a.m. to 12:27 p.m. on Oct. 27, and that it detected the intrusion at 12:14 p.m. that day. The revised timeline means the attacker went unnoticed for more than two weeks. Bithumb first reported that the data of 6,444 customers and 715 employees, or 7,159 people in total, had been exposed. It did not give an updated count on Wednesday. The notice lists customers, employees of partner companies and current and former staff among those affected. Passports, bank accounts and wallet addresses The list of exposed data now runs to 19 items. It includes member numbers, names, mobile numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, resident registration numbers, passport numbers and driver’s license numbers. It also covers bank account numbers, home addresses, gender, nationality, copies of ID documents, occupations, employer names and work contact details, as well as transaction histories and wallet addresses. Bithumb said not every item applies to every person, and that affected users will be told individually by email and text message what was taken. For crypto users, the wallet addresses and transaction records stand out. Paired with names and phone numbers, that kind of data can help scammers target people they know hold digital assets. Bithumb said Daou Office is an internal business system separate from customer exchange accounts and asset data. Bithumb promises compensation The exchange said it blocked the attacker’s IP addresses, fixed the vulnerability behind the incident and is running a security review of all of its externally exposed services. One project translates bitcoin terminology into 21 African languages. Another mines bitcoin with surplus solar power in rural Nigerian homes, paying it directly to the households that generate it. Others build tools for people facing repression anywhere — activists who need to find and fix the privacy leaks in their bitcoin use, communities who need self-custody devices built from parts found in any electronics store, observers who need election evidence preserved before it disappears, and people who need to turn an ordinary phone into an offline Bitcoin wallet. Together, these efforts help human rights defenders, journalists, nonprofits, and individuals hold, send, and verify their money freely under repression. CryoBrick transforms feature phones into offline Bitcoin signing devices. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? sports.title: Stuttgart wasteful again as Sucic and Lautaro seal Inter win
sports.description: Stuttgart wasteful again as Sucic and Lautaro seal Inter win As Stuttgart looked to get back to winning ways in Europe following the defeat to Galatasaray, they could hardly have gotten off to a more encouraging start, with the visitors testing Italian giants Inter in the early stages. Maximilian Mittelstädt fired in a teasing ball after six minutes, flying a matter of centimetres past the foot of Ermedin Demirovic. The Bosnian forward, and skipper on the night, would be presented with an opportunity again just over a minute later, linking up well with Chris Führich before seeing a shot blocked. Führich, who was Stuttgart's best player in Istanbul before the international break, remained at the heart of proceedings, seeing an effort well saved by Josep Martinez on the half-volley, before Djed Spence was denied by Dennis Seimen at the other end following the resulting corner. And after the strong Stuttgart start, it would be all Inter for the rest of the half, with Marcus Thuram and Nicolo Barella having the best chances - the former hitting the side netting after a poor Finn Jeltsch backpass, while Barella struck the post with a lovely outside-of-the-boot effort inside the box. Tailing off after the positive start, Stuttgart were looking to avoid the sloppiness that plagued the half outside of the opening 15 minutes. However, after the opening minutes matched the theme of the first half, Inter would be presented with a huge chance to open the scoring, when Federico Dimarco's cross struck the hand of Josha Vagnoman, resulting in a penalty for the hosts after a VAR check. And with a hop and a skip, Petar Sucic would wrong-foot Seimen, sending the ball straight down the middle and giving the Nerazzurri the lead on home soil. Reacting well, Nikolas Nartey would see an effort somehow saved off the line from a corner, while the visitors began to finally regain some of their attacking impetus. Führich and Vagnoman were withdrawn, replaced by Deniz Undav and Jamie Leweling, while Angelo Stiller and Luca Jaquez followed, But just as they were beginning to threaten, with wing-back Mittelstädt calling for a penalty at one end, Inter went up the other end and doubled their lead through the ever-talismanic Lautaro Martinez, who hammered home off the post, catching a bouncing ball ever so sweetly to net his third goal in three Champions League outings. Sebastian Hoeneß cannot argue that the three points deservedly stay in Milan, but once again, he will have to deal with the frustrating topic of his side once again being wasteful. As a result, Stuttgart sit 17th in the standings, with a strong run to the end of the league phase in need, starting with the visit of Lille in two weeks time.

sports.title: 2 goals, 84% passing accuracy: Bruno Fernandes’ efforts go to waste as Man United held 2-2 by Sporting
sports.description: 2 goals, 84% passing accuracy: Bruno Fernandes’ efforts go to waste as Man United held 2-2 by Sporting Manchester United were held to a 2-2 draw by Sporting at the Estádio José Alvalade on Wednesday, 25 November, in the Champions League. A Bruno Fernandes brace was cancelled out by two goals from Luis Suárez in an entertaining game that earned Mauricio Pochettino his first points since taking charge at Old Trafford. The Argentine made four changes to the team that was thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield last weekend in the Premier League. Matheus Cunha missed the game due to suspension, while Diogo Dalot, Matthijs de Ligt and Patrick Dorgu all dropped to the bench. Harry Maguire and Noussair Mazraoui came into the team, starting at the back alongside Leny Yoro and Lisandro Martínez. Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans retained their place in the starting XI, continuing their partnership in midfield. Bruno Fernandes continued in the No. 10 position, with Bryan Mbeumo moving to the left forward role and Amad starting on the right. Joshua Zirkzee started for the first time this season, operating in the No. 9 role. United secure hard-fought draw United had a bright start, but Sporting gradually got a grip on the game. Martínez conceded a penalty, which was saved by Senne Lammens in the 30th minute. However, the Belgian conceded a penalty moments later, which was successfully converted by Luis Suárez in the 33rd minute. The visitors pushed for an equaliser late in the second half, but went into the break trailing 1-0. Martínez made amends early in the second half, winning a penalty which Fernandes converted in the 48th minute. The United skipper then scored a second two minutes later, giving his team the lead. Sporting pushed for an equaliser and finally found one through Suárez in the 80th minute following a Lammens error. United did have the ball in the back of the net late in the game but it was ruled out by VAR. The game ended 2-2, despite the best efforts of Fernandes, who sizzled on his return to his former hunting ground. Page 1 of 5 1 2 3 4 5 Fernandes decisive on Sporting return Bruno Fernandes played the entire 90 minutes on his return to the Estádio José Alvalade, before being replaced in the second half injury time, managing 49 touches of the ball. The Portuguese maestro attempted 44 passes with an 84% accuracy rate. The 32-year-old attempted two crosses and one long ball, but none of them found a teammate. Surprisingly, Fernandes did not register a single key pass in the game. The Portuguese attempted two tackles and was dribbled past once in the game. Fernandes won three of his six duels but lost the ball 13 times. However, it was in the final third where Fernandes crucially made his presence felt. The United skipper registered two shots on target, both of which ended up in the back of the net. He also registered another shot off target, a free-kick that narrowly missed the far post.

sports.title: Pavlovic drops clanger as Lille seal upset win vs Bayern
sports.description: Pavlovic drops clanger as Lille seal upset win vs Bayern On a night in which Bayern Munich were looking to reset the mood after a week of injuries and controversy behind the scenes, Vincent Kompany would be left to field a far-from-ideal lineup with multiple stars watching on from the sidelines. Konrad Laimer's versatility has been well-documented throughout his years in the Bundesliga, but few could have predicted that the Austrian would be the man to start up top in Lille. And much to their credit, the German record champions did not have to get out of second gear in the first half, despite the rather makeshift lineup. Dayot Upamecano would open the scoring in Northern France after just 15 minutes, rising highest to meet Tom Bischof's corner to head home from six yards out. From then on, Bayern were cruising, before the half-time break completely turned the tide. Lille would see an equaliser disallowed after just a minute of second-half football, when Ayase Ueda bundled over Joshua Kimmich in the build-up to the latter scoring an own goal. But the Mastiffs remained well in the occasion before Ueda netted an equaliser in the 60th minute, and it is hard to say it wasn't deserved after a much better start to the second period. And within a matter of moments, the hosts would take the lead when Ethan Mbappe raced through on goal just to find the post, before Aleksandar Pavlovic bundled the ball into his own net following an attempt to control the ball he will not want to see again. Out of nowhere, Lille had a huge upset win in their sights, while Bayern turned to Luis Diaz and Jamal Musiala from the bench, and campus graduates Tim Binder and Noah Codjo-Evore made their European debuts. Soriba Diaoune missed a huge chance to add a third on the volley five minutes out from time, ensuring that the final moments were going to remain uncomfortable for the hosts. But, as much as the makeshift Bayern frontline threw at Lille in the closing stages, the French side were able to hold on for what is a huge win - their first of the Champions League season. Bayern, on the other hand, tasted defeat for the first time in all competitions this term, seeing the rather strange week continue for the record champions.

sports.title: Former Packers QB claimed by Arizona Cardinals
sports.description: (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kedon Slovis has had quite a journey this season. Slovis, who started the year with the Arizona Cardinals, was released by the team at the cutdown deadline, then picked up by the Green Bay Packers’ practice squad — after the Packers traded Kyle McCord to the Miami Dolphins. Slovis spent two months in Green Bay before the Baltimore Ravens poached him, then had to guarantee him three weeks on the active roster before they could release him — per NFL rules. While Lamar Jackson hasn’t returned to the lineup for the Ravens, Baltimore has since made a trade that has adjusted their quarterback room: Adding former Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett. With Brissett starting, the Ravens waived Slovis yesterday, and he’s now back in Arizona — his third overall stint with the LaFleur brothers this season. Slovis joins rookie Carson Beck, veteran journeyman Josh Johnson and Joey Aguilar, who was poached from the Jacksonville Jaguars’ practice squad in Week 10, with the Cardinals. Injuries have led to an interesting quarterback carousel this season, and it’s only going to get more interesting now that Aaron Rodgers is on the market . With Slovis off the table for the Packers, assume that they’ll stick with Cam Miller on the practice squad for the time being.

Another commonality between those seasons is that the Lakers won at least 54 regular season games (or the equivalent of it in an 82-game season in the case of the pandemic-shortened 2019-20) each time they had such a hot start to the season. technology.description: American water systems are even less secure than we thought, according to a study of 236 technology vendors that provide gear to US drinking water, wastewater, and industrial water systems. The federal government has issued 4,014 security advisories for industrial control systems and cataloged 1,792 vulnerabilities known to have been exploited in cyberattacks. A new index, called Water Supply Chain Watch and published by exposure management firm Securin, however, found almost twice as many vulnerabilities as public records identified – including 20 exploited flaws that weren't even in the federal government's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The security provider compared data on water-tech vendors with records from the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the FBI, and WaterISAC, drawing on CISA advisory data through November 20 and KEV catalog entries through November 23. It found that federal water advisories hit their highest level this year since 2020. However, the volume of security alerts isn't a reliable predictor of real-world attacks, the researchers noted. Five vendors – Rockwell Automation (58), Advantech (48), Schneider Electric (35), Siemens (26), and ABB (24) – account for 191 of the 376 water-tagged security advisories. The No. 2 firm, Advantech, accounted for the highest number of vulnerabilities rated critical, but none of the CVEs in its advisories appear in CISA's KEV catalog. Unitronics, on the other hand, accounted for only two water-tagged security advisories, but at least 75 of its controllers were compromised between November 2023 and January 2024 by attackers taking advantage of default or missing passwords. The report also highlights another disconnect between water-related CVEs and real-world cyberattacks, which don't always require attackers to exploit software bugs. The July intrusions, which security researchers suspect were the work of Iran-linked attackers , targeted more than 100 water systems , with incidents reported across at least 12 states , and involved poorly secured internet-connected controllers . According to Securin, 791 Rockwell MicroLogix 1400 controllers across multiple industries in the US were exposed to the internet as of November 17. technology.title: Huawei and crew tout homegrown EDA tools to overcome China’s fab deficit
technology.description: Chinese telecom and IT giant Huawei boasted about its advancements in domestic electronic design automation (EDA) software this week, which it needs to accelerate the adoption of homegrown chip manufacturing. EDA is an umbrella term for software, hardware, and services essential to the planning, design, and production of modern chips. Today, Cadence Design Systems, Synopsys, and Siemens dominate the industry, but US export controls have restricted Huawei and other blacklisted Chinese businesses' access to their tools. The US blacklisted Huawei back in 2019 over concerns the telecommunications equipment giant could be forced to inject backdoors into its gear. Unable to access top EDA tools, Huawei’s chip division, HiSilicon, was forced to develop its own with the help of Phlexing Technology. This week, Phlexing chairman Qing He detailed the company’s efforts to bring new EDA tools to support Huawei’s so-called Tau Scaling Law design philosophy. “Tau EDA is the domestic EDA tool chain for Tau chips. It comes from a long, close partnership with Huawei,” he said. We discussed the tech earlier this year, but in a nutshell, it involves using advanced packaging, specifically 3D hybrid bonding, to achieve higher transistor density for a given area. The TSMC of China, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), is still years behind Taiwan, South Korea, and the US on process technology. It currently has the ability to mass-produce chips on the equivalent of a 7 nm process. For comparison, TSMC began producing 5 nm-class products in 2020 and commenced mass production of 2 nm-class chips in late 2025. So, Huawei aims to use 3D packaging to close the gap, but for this to happen, it first needs tools capable of designing such chips, and that’s just what Phlexing claims to have done with its GloryBolt and GloryEX platforms. “Traditional EDA has long handled only single processes. Tau EDA needs to integrate and decompose multiple processes,” He said. “Coupling multi-scale, multi-structure, and multi-physics issues called for new analysis tools.” This, He says, culminated in the co-development of a process design kit (PDK) with Huawei beginning in 2024. These technologies have now gone live. The development comes as Huawei looks to bring larger, more capable processors to market. We previously discussed the company’s latest developments around AI accelerators, near packaged optics, networking, and rack systems. Many of these advancements will depend on multi-die chip packages, enabled by EDA tools, like those built by Phlexing. ®

technology.title: Hera probe finds DART left a stadium-sized dent in asteroid Dimorphos
technology.description: The European Space Agency's Hera probe has revealed a stadium-sized crater on Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA struck with its DART spacecraft in 2022. The Double Asteroid Redirection Test was deliberately crashed into the asteroid on September 26, 2022. The original plan called for a European spacecraft – Asteroid Impact Mission (AIM) – to launch first and observe the before and after effects of DART. AIM was canceled, and the Hera mission launched in 2024. DART was a success. Scientists were able to determine that the impact had indeed changed the orbit of Dimorphos. The question was what else had happened to the asteroid. Scientists spotted ejecta and debris following the DART impact, but the close-up observations by Hera have revealed the full extent of the collision. Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at CNRS / Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur, said: "Scientists debated whether Dimorphos had sustained an impact crater, changed its shape or stayed the same. "Much to our surprise the answer turns out to be all three at once! The face struck by DART has been flattened into an impact crater the size of a sports stadium, which extends across the asteroid's entire width." Scientists also noted that the asteroid is now tumbling in its orbit. Hera is surveying the 151-meter-wide Dimorphos and its larger companion, the 730-meter-wide Didymos, from about 25 to 30 km away. It moves around the pair at roughly 12 cm/s, using thruster firings to trace rectangular paths rather than conventional circular orbits. The plan is to approach closer, to about 13 km, to get higher-resolution snaps. A complicating factor is the discovery that hundreds of orbiting boulders surround the asteroids. Michael Kueppers, ESA's Hera mission scientist, said: "The team will have to take account of these objects in the coming weeks as the mission moves in closer." Hera will deploy two CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, in early 2027. The Italian-led Milani will study surface composition and surrounding dust, while the Luxembourg-led Juventas will use radar to probe Dimorphos's interior before attempting a landing. Scientists also want to measure Dimorphos's mass. Combined with the observed change in its orbit, that will help them assess how effectively DART transferred momentum to the asteroid and improve predictions for future deflection attempts. Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli said: "NASA's DART mission demonstrated that we can change an asteroid's orbit. Hera is now revealing what happened to the asteroid itself. By combining these two missions, humanity is taking a decisive step towards making asteroid deflection a reliable tool for protecting our planet." ®

technology.title: Microsoft's NTLM security changes trip up third-party logins
technology.description: Microsoft's November security updates can break authentication in some third-party applications and devices following changes to NTLM message signing. Affected systems include authentication proxy servers, single sign-on (SSO) products, and application packaging tools, the company's support notice says. The failures stem from products that claim to supply required information during NTLM authentication but return incomplete or empty data, Microsoft said: "An affected device might set the NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_TARGET_INFO flag in its CHALLENGE_MESSAGE but provide an empty or incomplete TargetInfo field." Administrators can use the notice's network trace and event log examples to identify affected products. For confirmed cases, the temporary workaround is to set the ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm Registry value to 1 on affected clients. This stops the client offering signing, backing out the new default rather than fixing the incompatible product. The recommended long-term options are a vendor update or Kerberos authentication, where supported. The value sits under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 and defaults to 0, enabling clients to offer signing on non-anonymous connections. The NTLM changes arrived in the November 10 update as phase 1 in a 2-phase process. In phase 1, "Windows client devices begin offering NTLM signing on all connections by default. Servers accept both signed and unsigned clients. Auditing events identify clients not using signing." Phase 2, scheduled for May 2027, will make Windows servers require NTLM signing by default. "Clients that do not offer signing will be rejected by secure servers," Microsoft stated. Ominously, Microsoft warned that it "might remove the registry keys at a future date," so the company is not kidding about the temporary workaround thing. The additional protections were added to address CVE-2026-118737 , a vulnerability in which "improper verification of cryptographic signature in Windows Remote Procedure Call Runtime allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network." NTLM is on Microsoft's hit list, having joined the Deprecated Features list in 2024. It dates back to the era of Windows NT, and Microsoft has made clear that it wants customers to move to Kerberos, which became the default in 2000. Even so, NTLM lingers on. Deprecation doesn't remove Microsoft's obligation to secure NTLM while it remains in supported Windows releases. For administrators, though, the immediate task is identifying incompatible products before temporary exceptions give way to stricter enforcement. ®

technology.title: Ars Live recap: Don’t expect military attacks on data centers to stop
technology.description: Drone attacks on data centers. Amazon data centers came under military attack for the first time ever in the Middle East this year, and Russia and Ukraine exchanged an unprecedented flurry of drone strikes on each other’s data centers. To examine what such attacks on data centers mean for the future of cloud services that all modern societies depend upon, Ars hosted a live discussion. In a conversation with Ars Technica Tech Reporter Jeremy Hsu, Joseph Jarnecki at the Royal United Services Institute first talked about why public cloud data centers have increasingly become military targets during the 2026 Iran war and the ongoing full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine: We see an increasing acknowledgement and fact of dual use in particularly the public cloud, but also just across the board in private cloud data centers as well. The dual use that I refer to is the utilization of compute functions within these data centers—within cloud services—by militaries, for example, to run battlefield management systems, to do their HR, to do their resource management. Once a military uses a piece of civilian infrastructure, at least under international law or in terms of the principles of targeting that are taken forward by militaries, it can sometimes become a military object and is therefore of interest to an adversary, and there's an incentive to target it. technology.title: US Treasury financial crimes unit becomes latest fed breach victim
technology.description: The US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has taken some systems offline following unauthorized access, disrupting regulatory filings for financial institutions. An alert has gone up on FinCEN's Bank Secrecy Act E-Filing website, as shown in this archived copy , informing those who need to submit reports that they might not be able to while the agency deals with the situation. FinCEN not only enforces compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act and associated regulations but also collects and analyzes financial intelligence for sharing with other US agencies and foreign government partners. In other words, it has some juicy info in its databases. “FinCEN is investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems,” the alert states. “As a proactive measure, FinCEN has taken some systems offline.” FinCEN hasn't said which systems intruders accessed, but clues in the deadline extension notice the agency posted alongside the warning suggest the disruption affects its reporting services for banks and other financial institutions required to submit reports detailing certain financial transactions and suspicious activity that may indicate money laundering or other illicit activity. FinCEN's Secure Data Transfer Mode, one method of submitting those reports, appears to be affected, as do services companies use to submit beneficial ownership information reports and individuals use to update their FinCEN identifiers. Eligible organizations and individuals with filings or updates due from November 18 through December 29 now have until December 30 to submit them. The Register has learned that there’s no evidence of any unauthorized access to Bank Secrecy Act data or beneficial ownership databases. That said, the investigation is ongoing - so that could change. “Treasury is working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and third-party forensic examiners to determine the scope and impact of the incident,” a FinCEN official told us in an email. Several US government agencies have experienced cybersecurity incidents in recent months, including the ATF and the FBI , and reports emerged this week that intruders had also compromised an unclassified CIA system . While US authorities have linked previous cyberespionage campaigns to Chinese or other government-backed groups , financially motivated criminal groups have also targeted federal agencies. As the FinCEN breach is still under investigation, the agency hasn’t stated who may be involved and for what purpose. ®

science.title: December full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Cold Moon
science.description: null The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon).. According to the late, great astronomer Fred Espenak , the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026! When to see the December full moon The full Cold Supermoon will make for a spectacular sight when it rises over the eastern horizon at sunset on Dec. 23, mere hours before reaching maximum illumination. Remember to use Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location. Earth's satellite may appear larger than normal while close to the horizon. This is partly because it is near perigee, when it appears subtly larger in the night sky, but also because of a phenomenon called the moon illusion, which tricks us into perceiving the moon to be bigger than it actually is while in the presence of foreground objects. A yellow full moon rises over Italy. (Image credit: Photo by Lorenzo Di Cola/NurPhoto via Getty Images) The moon may also adopt a striking golden or orange hue around moonrise and moonset. When the moon is low on the horizon, its light travels through more of Earth's atmopshere, scattering shorter, bluer wavelengths of light and allowing longer, redder wavelengths to reach our eyes. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
science.description: null On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights. The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet. NASA's M2-F3 lifting body drops from its carrier plane during a test flight in 1970. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered In the late 1960s and early 1970s, NASA was investigating lifting bodies as an approach to both new aircraft and what future spacecraft, and as its number suggests, the M2-F3 was not the first of its kind. In fact, the M2-F3 was a rebuilt version of its predecessor, the M2-F2 lifting body , after that vehicle crashed in a dry lake bed in California's Mojave Desert during an unpowered test flight. That crash (which appears in the opening of the TV show "The Six-Million-Dollar Man") led to upgrades for a better handling lifting body, NASA said. "When the M2-F2 was rebuilt and redesignated the M2-F3, it was modified with an additional third vertical fin – centered between the tip fins – to improve control characteristics," NASA wrote in an overview . Unpowered glide flights for the M2-F3 began in June 1970, but Dana's flight on Nov. 25 of that year was the first time the vehicle fired up its rocket engine to test its controls under powered flight. One vital upgrade on the vehicle was a set of reaction control thrusters to help maintain its orientation. "A reaction jet control system, similar to thrusters used on orbiting spacecraft, was also installed on the M2-F3 to obtain research data about their effectiveness for vehicle control," NASA wrote . "As the M2-F3’s portion of the lifting body program neared an end, it evaluated a rate command augmentation control system and a side-arm control stick similar to side-arm controllers now used on many modern aircraft." If you want, you can see the M2-F3 vehicle today. NASA donated it to the Smithsonian Institution. It is now hanging at the National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: NASA Enhances Supplier Program, Announces Mentor-Protégé Agreement
science.description: NASA’s Office of Small Business Programs (OSBP) hosted a ceremonial Mentor-Protégé Agreement signing between The Boeing Company and GRACE Aerospace on Oct. 29, 2026, at the U.S. Space and Rocket Center in Huntsville, Alabama. Pictured in the front row, from left to right, are Pauline Sevigny, president and owner, GRACE Aerospace; Christian Diamond, Mentor-Protégé Program manager, The Boeing Company; and Dwight Deneal, assistant administrator, OSBP. Pictured in the back row, from left to right, are Danielle Barnes, small business specialist, OSBP; Grant Crawford, Logan Ojermark, Nikki Howard, and Sabrina Pearson, contracting officers, NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) stages team; Christen Edwards, lead, SLS stages team; Bradley Niese, NASA’s senior procurement executive, deputy chief acquisition officer, and assistant administrator, Office of Procurement; Chris Hall, program manager, OSBP; and Kristina Parmenter, procurement officer, NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center. Credit: Justin Fields, Light Rain Studio How NASA works with small businesses is evolving, and as a result, the agency is strengthening the domestic aerospace industrial base to support future exploration missions through its recently renamed Small Business Supplier Development Program. As part of the program, NASA announced its latest Mentor-Protégé Agreement, this one signed between The Boeing Company and GRACE Aerospace. NASA is streamlining the application process for the Small Business Supplier Development Program, as well as reducing administrative requirements, accelerating review and approval timelines, and enhancing incentives for prime contractor participation. These improvements are aimed at making supplier development more accessible, efficient, and closely aligned with NASA’s mission needs. “We have intentionally redesigned the program as a mission-focused tool for strengthening industrial base readiness and mission success,” said Dwight Deneal, assistant administrator, Office of Small Business Programs, NASA Headquarters in Washington. “By simplifying participation and focusing developmental assistance on the capabilities NASA needs most, we are helping build a stronger, more resilient supplier base that can support the agency’s highest-priority missions.” Under the new Mentor-Protégé Agreement, Boeing will provide structured assistance to help GRACE expand its capabilities as a supplier of mission-critical aerospace hardware. Boeing will fund the agreement, valued at nearly $500,000. “Boeing is proud to continue its longstanding relationship with NASA in support of its mission and the opportunities this agreement creates for Boeing, GRACE, and the broader aerospace industrial base,” said Christian Diamond, Mentor-Protégé Program manager and small business liaison officer for Boeing. “Through this partnership, Boeing looks forward to sharing our expertise to support the continued growth and long-term success of a small business while strengthening our supplier base.”

science.title: Seabird ‘spies’ could help spot ships that aren’t broadcasting their location
science.description: A northern gannet ( Morus bassanus ) tagged with biologging devices on its back and tail Steve Votier Audio from seabirds fitted with mini recording devices and GPS trackers has been used by researchers to show that marine life can record encounters with vessels that are otherwise difficult to track. Many large vessels are now legally required to carry automatic identification systems broadcasting their identity and location at regular intervals. Although this has allowed interactions between animals and fisheries to be studied at scale, there are enormous gaps in coverage. In fact, recent research suggests that three-quarters of industrial fishing vessels don’t use the technology, says Jonathan Rutter at the University of Oxford. This is partly because regulations on the types of vessels that are required to share data vary by country. Large satellite ‘blind spots’ also contribute to the problem, he says, and so does subterfuge for the purpose of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing (IUU). Advertisement Read more Most large fishing boats go untracked as ‘dark vessels’ Rutter says that being caught as bycatch in fishing is one of the greatest risks to seabird populations, but if fishing vessels are only tracked “with conventional methods, such footprints of risk may be strikingly incomplete”. The team analysed audio collected from devices attached to seven northern gannets ( Morus bassanus ) and found that one third of the audio detections couldn’t be matched with vessel tracking data – mostly off the UK coast. Overall, 12 per cent of the vessel detections made by the four critically endangered Balearic shearwaters ( Puffinus mauretanicus ) included in the study couldn’t be matched to public data. But given the high vessel density where they were – off the Catalan coast – the researchers estimated that up to 20 per cent of the vessels detected by the four birds weren’t broadcasting their identity. Tammy Davies at BirdLife International – a global partnership of non-governmental organisations – who wasn’t involved in the study, says the research could “give us a more complete picture of the risks seabirds face at sea” and “ultimately, this could contribute to better assessments of bycatch risk and help identify fisheries and areas where conservation measures are most needed”. Peter Ejbye-Ernst at the Netherlands Institute for the Study of Crime and Law Enforcement (NSCR), describes the study as “fascinating” from a green criminology point of view, too.
